summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Cloning vectors require an Ori (copy number control), selectable markers (ampR, tetR), and unique restriction sites. pBR322 contains ampR (Pst I/Pvu I), tetR (Bam HI/Sal I), and Rop (Pvu II). Disarmed Ti plasmids (Agrobacterium) transform plants, while disarmed retroviruses transform mammals.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 3.1 Four Essential Features of Cloning Vectors
1. **Origin of Replication (Ori)**: DNA sequence where replication initiates. Any foreign DNA ligated to this sequence replicates along with the vector. It determines and controls the **copy number** of the plasmid ($15\text{--}20\text{ to }100\text{ copies/cell}$).
2. **Selectable Marker Genes**: Genes encoding resistance to antibiotics (e.g., *ampicillin*, *tetracycline*, *kanamycin*, *chloramphenicol*) that allow selective growth and identification of transformants while eliminating non-transformed cells.
3. **Unique Restriction Sites (Multiple Cloning Site / MCS)**: Vector must possess single, unique recognition sites for common restriction enzymes. Multiple sites for a single enzyme would cut the vector into multiple fragments, complicating gene cloning.
4. **Small Molecular Size**: Low molecular weight facilitates easy extraction, laboratory manipulation, and high transformation efficiency into host cells.

### 3.2 Anatomy of Plasmid pBR322 ($4361\text{ bp}$)
- Engineered artificial plasmid designed by **Bolivar and Rodriguez**.
- **$amp^R$ (Ampicillin Resistance Gene)**: Contains unique restriction sites for ***Pst I*** and ***Pvu I***.
- **$tet^R$ (Tetracycline Resistance Gene)**: Contains unique restriction sites for ***Bam HI*** and ***Sal I***.
- **$Eco\text{ RI}$, $Cla\text{ I}$, $Hind\text{ III}$ Sites**: Located upstream outside the resistance genes.
- **$Rop$ Gene**: Encodes the *Repressor of Priming* protein involved in regulating plasmid replication copy number; contains a unique site for ***Pvu II***.

### 3.3 Plant & Animal Cloning Vectors
- **Plant Vector (The Ti Plasmid)**: ***Agrobacterium tumefaciens*** ("Nature's Genetic Engineer") naturally transfers its **T-DNA** segment from the **Ti (Tumor-Inducing) Plasmid** into dicot plant genomes, forming crown gall tumors. The plasmid is *disarmed* by removing oncogenic genes while retaining the T-DNA borders to shuttle beneficial genes.
- **Mammalian Vector (Disarmed Retroviruses)**: Retroviruses capable of transforming normal animal cells into cancerous cells are *disarmed* and repurposed as gene delivery vehicles for mammalian cell culture and human gene therapy.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Cosmids and BACs
conceptBreakdown.title: Cosmids and BACs
conceptBreakdown.content: Cosmids (plasmids containing bacteriophage lambda cos sites) accept inserts up to 45 kb; Bacterial Artificial Chromosomes (BACs) and Yeast Artificial Chromosomes (YACs) clone large genomic fragments up to 300 kb and 1 Mb respectively for genome sequencing.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Expression Vectors vs Cloning Vectors
conceptBreakdown.title: Expression Vectors vs Cloning Vectors
conceptBreakdown.content: Cloning vectors are optimized for DNA propagation and gene sequencing; Expression vectors contain strong inducible promoters (e.g., T7, lac), ribosomal binding sites (Shine-Dalgarno), and transcription terminators to drive high-level recombinant protein synthesis.
